title: Training-free Spatially Grounded Geometric Shape Encoding
claim: A family of orthogonal basis functions on the unit disk, indexed by two integer modes, spans increasingly fine radial and angular patterns.
layout: 3x3 grid of disks, row-major, shared diverging colorbar at right
description: A 3x3 grid of circular heatmaps. Each disk is a real-part Zernike basis function on the unit disk, with a title in italic math above it giving radial order n and angular frequency m. The titles run from n=0,m=0 to n=6,m=4. The first disk is a uniform salmon color. The next ones show a left-right split, then a concentric ring pattern, and a saddle or X pattern. The later disks show more lobes and finer angular and radial structure. A vertical red-white-blue diverging colorbar on the right runs from -1.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 at white. Red marks positive values and blue marks negative values. The eye goes first to the colorful lobed disks, and the pattern gets more complex toward the bottom right.
caption: Zernike basis visualization, we visualize nine real-part basis governed by radial mode 𝑛 and angular frequency 𝑚.
abstract: In this work, we introduce a novel training-free encoding framework, dubbed XShapeEnc , that encodes an arbitrary spatially grounded 2D geometric shape into a compact representation exhibiting five favorable properties, including invertibility, adaptivity, generality and controllability. Specifically, a 2D spatially grounded geometric shape is decomposed into its normalized geometry within the unit disk and its pose vector, where the pose is further transformed into a harmonic pose field that also lies within the unit disk. A set of orthogonal Zernike basis is constructed to encode shape geometry and pose either independently or jointly, with controllable relative emphasis on shape geometry or shape pose. We demonstrate the theoretical validity, efficiency, discriminability, and wide applicability of XShapeEnc via extensive analysis and experiments across a wide range of shape-aware tasks and our self-curated XShapeCorpus dataset. We envision XShapeEnc as a foundational framework for encoding tasks beyond one-dimensional discrete data and data-driven, learning-based paradigms, paving the way for unified and trained-free spatial encoding framework design.
